newsitem.title: USA: Mistrial declared on most Spokane bombing charges.
newsitem.headline: Mistrial declared on most Spokane bombing charges.

text.p: A federal jury on Wednesday convicted three Idaho men of having illegal weapons and stolen vehicles, but a mistrial was declared on charges they carried out bank robberies and bombings last year.

After more than three days of deliberations, the jury reported they were unable to come to a verdict on the most serious charges against the men, charged with robbing a Spokane area bank branch twice and setting off three bombs in an apparent diversion.

Verne Jay Merrell, 51, Charles Barbee, 45, and Robert Berry, 42, all of the Sandpoint, Idaho, area, were convicted of possessing the illegal weapons and stolen vehicles when they were arrested in October near Yakima.
U.S. District Judge Frem Nielsen declared a mistrial on the other charges.
Prosecutors said they had not decided whether to retry the men, but Roger Peven, attorney for Barbee, said he expected a new trial.
A note from the jury Monday indicated the jury was split 11-1, but Peven said he did not have details.
